title: Resuming Overpayment Recovery after a Dispute Decision — Network Participation Agreements
content:
This rule of the **Network Participation Agreements** covers the first withholding Cascade books against a claim payment run to recover an overpayment after a dispute decision upheld it in full or reduced it. It covers only that first post-decision withholding; later withholdings of the same overpayment are continuing run withholdings.

## Scope among the practice's agreements

Overpayments are recovered at the level of the practice: an open overpayment under one agreement may be offset against remittances under any active or termination pending agreement of the same practice, except that a continuing capitation withholding, a continuing run withholding, a post-decision withholding and a plan installment each select only among the overpayments of the agreement whose payment they are withheld from, and only those four do.

## Order and limits of offsets

Open overpayments of the practice are offset oldest notice first, except that a continuing capitation withholding and a continuing run withholding go to the overpayment the agreement's most recent withholding was applied to, a post-decision withholding goes to the overpayment of the agreement's most recent dispute decision and a plan installment goes to the overpayment the plan down payment was recorded against, and only those four withholdings follow these selections instead of notice order; the total withheld from a claim payment run may not exceed the agreement type's recoupment percentage of that run's claim payments, while a withholding from a capitation payment is measured against the capitation amount itself, at the agreement type's recoupment percentage of it for the first withholding of an overpayment and at the continuing capitation withholding share for a continuing capitation withholding.

## When the withholding is fixed

A post-decision withholding is fixed only after the latest claim payment run carries the continuing run withholding owed on any overpayment under recovery whose notice is older than the decided overpayment's notice.

## Effect

The post-decision withholding is due once its conditions hold, and Cascade books it. It lowers the open amount of the decided overpayment by the amount withheld. It shows on the run's remittance advice as an amount withheld.

## Invocation: `book_decision_withholding_431b56e1`

**Capability.** The tool books the withholding that resumes recovery of an overpayment after the practice's dispute of it has been decided, upholding or reducing it. Cascade keeps part of a claim payment run toward the amount that stands. One call adds one withholding entry to the agreement's overpayment ledger.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `provider_agreement_id` | Reference number of the network participation agreement whose claim payment run is withheld from, as returned by the agreement lookup for the practice | Id |
| `original_payment_event_id` | Reference number of the decided overpayment notice entry, as returned by the provider payment and overpayment lookup or the dispute lookup for that agreement | Id |
| `remittance_number` | Remittance advice number of the claim payment run withheld from, copied character for character from the remittance entry, preserving every letter, digit and hyphen with no normalisation | Verbatim text |
| `withheld_amount` | Amount kept from the run | USD, positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent by the caller |

**Return.** A text rendering of a dictionary confirming the booking:

- `status`: the text "booked" when the withholding entry was added;
- `entry_id`: reference number of the new withholding entry;
- `provider_agreement_id`: echoed;
- `overpayment_case_number`: case number printed on the decided overpayment notice;
- `remittance_number`: echoed;
- `amount`: USD with 2 decimal places;
- `event_date`: date YYYY-MM-DD.
